- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; dampen forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply downward bias in second half of forecast window.
- Model underperforms in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; use 3–5 day moving average of recent history to anchor early forecast.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in correction.
